title: POST /:auditId/corrective-actions issues unique carReference under concurrent creation requests
steps: Fire 10 concurrent POST /api/audit-assurance/:auditId/corrective-actions requests against the same audit
Query the resulting CAR documents' carReference values
expectedResult: All 10 CARs are created with distinct carReference values (e.g. CAR-0001..CAR-0010 pattern) and no 500/duplicate-key error is surfaced to any caller.

title: Same user cannot submit-verification and then verify their own CAR end-to-end via the API
preconditions: A CAR exists with status='remediation_in_progress', assignedTo=userA
expectedResult: The submit-verification call succeeds (status becomes 'verification_pending'). The subsequent verify call by the same userA is rejected 403 'Verifier cannot be the same as the assignee (segregation of duties)'; status remains 'verification_pending'.

title: GET /api/audit-assurance/findings/search returns org-scoped results capped at 20 per page
description: searchFindingsGlobal (findings.controller.js:357) is registered ahead of the :auditId-scoped routes at audit-assurance.routes.js:374 and caps page size at Math.min(20, requestedLimit).
preconditions: Org has 30+ findings across multiple audits
steps: As an org user, call GET /api/audit-assurance/findings/search?limit=100
Inspect the returned page size and whether any finding from a different org appears
expectedResult: Response returns at most 20 findings regardless of the requested limit, and every returned finding belongs to the caller's organization.

title: Deleting an audit orphans its findings and CARs with no cascade check
description: Live defect H-002 in the Audit Assurance QA tracker: deleteAudit() performs no cascade check for existing AuditNonConformance rows (findings/CARs) referencing the audit before deleting it.
preconditions: An audit exists with at least one open finding and one open CAR
steps: As a user with audit.delete permission, call DELETE /api/audit-assurance/:auditId
Query AuditNonConformance for documents where auditId equals the deleted audit's id
expectedResult: Current behavior: the audit is deleted successfully and its findings/CARs remain in the database, now referencing a nonexistent auditId (orphaned) with no warning returned to the caller. Flag for remediation: deleteAudit() should either block deletion when open findings/CARs exist or cascade-soft-delete them.

title: GET /:auditId/management-reviews/input-data aggregates current CAR and finding state for the audit
preconditions: Audit has a mix of open and closed findings/CARs
expectedResult: Response includes counts/details reflecting the audit's current findings and CAR states so a management review meeting has accurate ISO 27001 Clause 9.3 input data to review.

title: PATCH finding allows a direct open->closed status change with no transition validation
description: updateFinding (findings.controller.js:255-311) writes req.body.status directly onto the document via FIELD_MAP with no check that the new value is a legal transition from the current status — unlike CARs, which have (a partial) CAR_VALID_TRANSITIONS check.
preconditions: A finding exists with status='open', recordType='finding'
steps: As a user with audit.update permission, call PATCH /:auditId/findings/:findingId with { status: 'closed' } in a single request, skipping any intermediate review/remediation state
expectedResult: Current behavior: the request succeeds and the finding's status jumps directly from 'open' to 'closed' with no server-side rejection. Flag for remediation: introduce a transition map for finding status analogous to CAR_VALID_TRANSITIONS.

title: POST /corrective-actions/escalate bumps escalationLevel monotonically based on daysOverdue thresholds
preconditions: A CAR exists past its targetClosureDate by an amount exceeding the 'manager' threshold in CAR_ESCALATION_THRESHOLDS_DAYS
expectedResult: The overdue CAR's escalationLevel moves from 'none'/'auditor' up to 'manager' (matching the configured threshold), and escalationLevel never moves backward on a subsequent call if the CAR becomes less overdue relative to a stale snapshot.

title: Mixed soft-delete conventions across audit_scope_items/audit_findings/audit_nonconformances produce inconsistent visibility of deleted records
description: Live defect H-003 (in-progress): audit_scope_items uses both isDeleted and deletedAt; the legacy audit_findings collection uses only isDeleted with no equivalent pre-find auto-filter hook; only audit_nonconformances is standardized on deletedAt with the pre(/^find/) hook.
preconditions: A soft-deleted document exists in each of AuditScopeItem, legacy AuditFinding, and AuditNonConformance
steps: Query each of the three collections/models using their respective default list method with no explicit deletedAt/isDeleted filter
Compare whether each correctly excludes its soft-deleted document
expectedResult: AuditNonConformance correctly excludes the soft-deleted row via its automatic pre-find hook. AuditScopeItem and the legacy AuditFinding model require the caller to remember the correct field name manually — document any query path that omits this and would leak a soft-deleted record.
